conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Let's begin. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you some questions about your child.

**First question: How old is your child?**

The age of your child is important because:
- Children **under 16** are generally automatically qualifying
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** are not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age (or if you have multiple children, we can go through each one).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 16 years old. He recently left school and has signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So Alex is 16 years old and has left school, and is currently signed up with the local careers service.

Since Alex is 16, we need to check if he meets the education or training requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current situation better. Since he's 16 and has left school:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as A-levels, vocational qualifications, apprenticeships, or other approved courses), OR
2. **Has he recently left education** (within the last few months)?

From what you've described, it sounds like he's left school and is working with the careers service but hasn't started any new education or training yet. 

**When did Alex leave school?** This is important because there may be a temporary extension period if he left recently (within the last 20 weeks).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school just a few weeks ago, actually. He finished in the summer and then registered with the careers service pretty much straight away to get some help deciding what to do next. He hasn't started any new course or training yet - he's still figuring things out.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying! So Alex left school just a few weeks ago (in the summer) and hasn't started any new education or training yet - he's registered with the careers service and is still deciding on his next steps.

Since he recently left education, let me check the extension eligibility rules that may apply in this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! This is very relevant to Alex's situation. There's a special **20-week extension** that can apply when a 16 or 17-year-old has recently left education.

Based on what you've told me:
- ✓ Alex is 16 (under 18)
- ✓ He left school just a few weeks ago (well within the 20-week period)
- ✓ He registered with the local careers service (which is a qualifying service)

This means Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension period! However, I need to check one more important condition:

**Is Alex working full-time?** 

For this purpose, "full-time work" means working 24 hours or more per week. Part-time work is fine, but if he's working 24+ hours per week, this would affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now. He's just been focusing on sorting out what he wants to do next with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is not working at all, he meets all the requirements for the extension period. Let me confirm this.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since Alex is not working at all (which means he's definitely working less than 24 hours per week), he passes this check. Let me move to the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question about Alex:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits claimed in his own name

This would not include any benefits that you as a parent receive for him, just benefits he might be claiming himself.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself. He doesn't get Universal Credit or ESA or anything like that in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own right. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

You mentioned he hasn't started any training yet, so I believe the answer is no - but I want to confirm. Most apprenticeships would affect eligibility, except for Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales which are approved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. Like I said, he hasn't started anything yet - he's still working with the careers service to figure out what direction he wants to go in.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so that's fine. Let me move to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency status. This is about where you (the claimant) live.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

There are various ways to meet the residency requirements:
- You normally live in the UK, OR
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, OR
- Other special circumstances apply (such as being a Crown servant abroad, or having pre-settled status with certain conditions)

For most people, if you live in the UK on a regular basis, you'll meet this requirement. Do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK (in Manchester), you meet the residency requirements. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about your responsibility for Alex. 

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means either:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You contribute to his upkeep (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards his care - this can include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.), OR
- You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Do you live with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex lives with you, you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Any other person

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming but you both agree that you should claim instead, that can be arranged. But if there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to decide.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, we can continue. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about Alex's living situation. You mentioned he lives at home with you, but I need to confirm if any special circumstances apply:

**Is Alex currently:**
- In hospital (for an extended period)?
- In local authority care?
- In a foster care arrangement?
- Or is he living normally at home with you?

From what you've told me, it sounds like he's living normally at home with you. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He's just living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is living normally at home with you, let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

For example, are they contributing to his housing costs or providing financial support for his care? This would be different from standard support services like the careers service he's using.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance. He's just living here with me as normal.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me process the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Good News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

Alex qualifies under the **20-week extension period** for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education. This special provision applies because:

✅ Alex is 16 years old (under 18)  
✅ He left school just a few weeks ago (well within the 20-week window)  
✅ He registered with the local careers service (a qualifying service)  
✅ He's not working full-time (less than 24 hours per week)  
✅ He's not receiving benefits like ESA or Universal Credit in his own right  
✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  

And you meet all the claimant requirements:  
✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you)  
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✅ The council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

### Important to Know:

The **20-week extension ends** either:
- When 20 weeks have passed since Alex left education, OR
- When Alex turns 18 (whichever comes first)

If Alex starts approved education or training before the extension expires, your Child Benefit can continue based on that new status.

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware**: If you or your partner earn over £60,000, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply (but you can still claim)
5. **Payments**: Made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**Apply here:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about claiming or anything else I can help clarify?
